units.translation: having thrown [something] at the courtyard gates
hear the sound at the courtyard door
net: on which meaning see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2033.
to keep back the irresistible wave of the sea with strong barriers
for when men exist, it is a secure fence
this nearest single-guardian enclosure of the Apian land
having seen him in the nets of Justice
rock, reef. Explained by grammarians as ὕφαλος πέτρα [submerged rock], on which meaning see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2034 2038.
It is singular, said of a burden to be carried in the womb.
ἕρμα [support, prop] as 'fence' (on which meaning see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2034) said of a tomb.
which the scholiast explains by βάρος [weight].
Hermann restored it for ἔρυμα [defense], which see.
having cast his former wealth upon the reef of Justice
where M has ἕρμαιον [a windfall], the copies correctly have ἑρμαῖον [of Hermes]: on which I have spoken in Lexico Soph. p. 191.
to the Hermaean crag of Lemnos
may the earth-rich race honor the Hermaean gift of the gods
the stranger seems to need a clear interpreter
ξυγκαταβῆναι νύχιόν θ᾽ Ἑρμῆν [to go down with the nocturnal Hermes], with the rest deleted, Hermann.
where M has ήερου, to which the corrector added his conjecture οἶμαι ἢ Ἑρμοῦ ῥάβδον [I think or the staff of Hermes], on which see under ῥάβδος [staff].
to us Hermes seems not to speak unseasonably
Hermes has brought us together with good reason
to go down with the chthonian and nocturnal Hermes
this is another Hermes, according to the laws of the Greeks
Argos, whom Hermes, the son of Earth, killed
to Hermes, the greatest patron and tracker
we honor Hermes as our ancestor
Hermes of the games, son of Maia and Zeus
to go down with the nocturnal Hermes
I think or the staff of Hermes
Thus more often the tragedians: see Thes. vol. 3 p. 2049.
and she, a stranger to a stranger, saved the shoot
such a shoot as no god could produce
Of adults: to go, to walk
which is said by tmesis for ὑφέρπει [creeps under].
corrupt from πρέπουσι [they are fitting]. See πρέπω [to be fitting].
and to the earth, dearest nurse; for she nourished the young creeping on her kindly soil
creep along the banks of this
uninvited, creeping as a feaster all day long
I go to the many-garlanded recess
and envious pain creeps upon the Atreidae, who are first in judgment

where I added ἔρρουσι [they perish], which is hidden in the letters ερα in M after ἄπαιδες [childless] v. 580, from which in the copies ἔρανται or ἔρρανται was made, which Hermann transferred to verse 571, changed to ἔρροντες [perishing] by Blomfield.
